title: Identification and Characterization of Rare Genetic Variants in Families with Severe Early Onset Periodontitis
summary: The aim of this study is to find out why some people develop a rare and severe form of periodontitis that begins very early in life, while others in the same family remain healthy. To this end, affected individuals with an onset of the disease up to the age of 20 and healthy relatives are included in the study. This makes it easier to investigate which genetic changes are linked to the disease and which are not. However, the age of participants at the time of the study does not affect their eligibility. All participants provide a saliva sample. The genetic material in this sample is examined to find possible changes associated with the disease. If certain changes are discovered, further tests are carried out to determine whether and how they affect the cells in the body. The aim of the study is to better understand why some people develop this severe form of periodontitis at a young age. The study will open up new possibilities for early detection and targeted treatment.
conditions: Early-onset severe periodontitis (Stage III-IV, Grade C; disease onset up to and including 20 years)

interventions.name: Patients with very early-onset severe periodontitis (EOPD; stage III/IV, grade C, onset ≤20 years). A saliva sample is taken for genetic testing (whole exome/genome sequencing) to identify rare disease-associated variants. For follow-up experiments, an additional blood or gingival tissue samples may
Relatives (1st and 2nd degree) of EOPD patients, regardless of periodontal status. Here, too, a single saliva sample is taken for genetic analysis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- severe periodontitis (stage III or IV, grade C)
- age of onset up to and including 20 years
- 1st and 2nd degree relatives regardless of diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
No biological relationship between the family members, e.g. in the case of adoption.
